body:
`aida awaiting`'s UNSHIPPED WORK rows render three different situations identically, and for TASK-1274 the displayed recovery command would REGRESS the PR I am holding. Verified by comparing commit subjects across branches, not by reading the rows.

ALL FOUR -rework BRANCHES ARE LOCAL-ONLY. task-1274-rework, task-1289-rework, bug-1288-rework, bug-1480-rework, bug-1480-rework2 have NO ref on origin (or on the gitlab mirror). Only the -work branches are pushed. So every one of these rows is reporting a branch that exists on exactly one machine.

THE DANGEROUS ONE - TASK-1274. The row reads:

    TASK-1274, task-1274-rework, 10 ahead, 1h, recovery: aida pr ship task-1274-rework

task-1274-rework contributes ZERO commits that PR #2019's branch lacks. The relationship is the inverse of what the row implies:

    subjects in task-1274-rework absent from the PR branch    0
    subjects on the PR branch absent from task-1274-rework    2

and the two it lacks are exactly the fixes that matter:

    [AI:claude] ci(gitlab): fix the notice-watchdog race that was actually failing the mirror's test job
    [AI:claude] ci(gitlab): inject the notice deadline instead of raising it globally

task-1274-rework is a STALE REBASED DUPLICATE (reflog: last rebased 13:41 today onto 42b7147bf0). Its ten commits are the same work by subject, at different shas. Running the displayed `aida pr ship task-1274-rework` would push a branch missing the notice-deadline fixes - the very defect the PR exists to correct.

WHY THE ROW CANNOT TELL. The "ahead" number is AHEAD-OF-MAIN. A stale duplicate of already-pushed work scores exactly as high as genuinely new work, because both are equally far from main. Ahead-of-main cannot distinguish "10 commits you have not shipped" from "10 commits you shipped already, under different shas, on a branch with a different name". The comparison that separates them is branch-vs-its-own-PR-head, which nothing computes.

THE OTHER THREE ARE NOT THE SAME SHAPE, which is the point - one rule will not cover them:

    BUG-1288    bug-1288-rework  strictly supersedes bug-1288-work (13 unique / 0)   -> hint is CORRECT, real unshipped work
    BUG-1480    bug-1480-rework2 strictly supersedes rework, which supersedes work    -> hint is CORRECT, rework2 is newest
    TASK-1289   NEITHER supersedes: rework has 20 unique subjects, work has 1         -> shipping EITHER drops something

TASK-1289's orphan commit is `[AI:codex] fix(lifecycle): keep express preflight enabled (TASK-1289)`, present on task-1289-work and absent from task-1289-rework. Ship rework and that fix is silently dropped; ship work and twenty commits are. The row offers `aida pr ship task-1289-rework` with no indication a commit is being left behind.

SO THE SURFACE IS RIGHT ABOUT 2 OF 4, ACTIVELY WRONG ABOUT 1, AND SILENTLY LOSSY ON 1. That is a worse profile than being wrong about all four, because two correct rows train you to trust the third.

WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING. I have not established WHY the duplicates exist - whether a drain created -rework after -work was already pushed, or a rebase was branched rather than forced. The reflog shows task-1274-rework created 12:18:56 and rebased twice, ending 13:41:34, but reflog is per-clone and I cannot see what other seat did what. That is a question for whoever ran those lanes, not an inference I should hand you as fact.

RELEVANCE TO MY SEAT: #2019 is the PR for TASK-1274, held at my CHANGES REQUESTED. I checked this precisely because an unshipped-rework row for a spec I am refusing is the shape of "rework landed and the reviewer never noticed" - STORY-1419's case. It turned out to be the opposite, which is the better outcome and the one I could not have assumed. My head sweep would never have caught either shape: it compares PR head to reviewed sha, and neither moves when work sits on a local branch.

Not filing, per the operator's standing directive. Your determination whether this is one row-level fix (compare against the spec's open PR head, not main) or the same class as STORY-1434 - a surface confidently rendering a state it cannot actually distinguish.
subject: aida awaiting's unshipped rows: 4 local-only branches, and the TASK-1274 recovery hint would ship work missing the notice-deadline fixes
